title: Clinical Bedside Teaching
path: Principles and Methods of Teaching in Midwifery

headings.title: Introduction to Clinical Bedside Teaching in Midwifery
headings.content: Clinical bedside teaching is a core instructional method used in Nigerian midwifery education to bridge theoretical knowledge and practical patient care. By interacting directly with mothers and newborns in the ward, student midwives observe real clinical presentations, practice communication skills, and develop professional judgment under direct supervision. Unlike classroom lectures, bedside teaching immerses learners in the authentic sights, sounds, and emotional realities of maternity units. It requires a delicate balance between providing quality student education and maintaining patient safety and comfort.

headings.title: Core Objectives of Teaching at the Patient's Bedside
headings.content: Teaching at the bedside aims to cultivate specific competencies that safe practitioners need in daily practice. Instructors use these sessions to teach systematic physical assessment, professional bedside manner, and clinical decision-making. Students learn how to interpret vital signs in context, take thorough obstetric histories, and communicate empathetically with women experiencing pain or anxiety. These objectives ensure that newly graduated midwives are clinically competent and emotionally attuned to their patients' needs.

headings.title: Preparing the Patient and Student for the Encounter
headings.content:
A successful bedside session begins long before the instructor and students step up to the patient's bed. Adequate preparation reduces anxiety for both the patient and the learner.

- **Patient Consent**: Always ask the patient for permission before involving students, ensuring she knows she can decline without affecting her care.
- **Briefing the Student**: Inform the learner of the clinical focus beforehand so they can review relevant anatomy or pathology.
- **Creating Psychological Safety**: Establish a supportive tone so students feel safe admitting what they do not know.

headings.title: Navigating Professional Ethics and Patient Dignity
headings.content: The patient's bed is her personal space, not a public stage. Midwifery instructors must model and enforce strict ethical standards during bedside encounters. Privacy screens must be drawn properly, and exposure of the patient's body must be kept to the absolute minimum necessary for the examination. Instructors must avoid talking about the patient as if she were absent or a mere specimen. Upholding dignity builds trust between the patient and the healthcare team.

headings.title: Facilitating Real-Time Constructive Feedback
headings.content: Feedback is most powerful when delivered close to the event. In bedside teaching, instructors can offer brief, targeted comments immediately after the student performs a task or interacts with a mother. To keep morale high, use the 'feedback sandwich' approach or focus first on what the student did well before correcting mistakes. Avoid criticizing students in front of the patient, as this undermines the patient's confidence in the learner's abilities.

headings.title: Common Challenges and Solutions in Busy Clinical Settings
headings.content: Nigerian maternity wards are often overcrowded, fast-paced, and understaffed. These realities make dedicated bedside teaching difficult. Noise, emergencies, and fatigued staff can disrupt planned tutorials. To overcome these barriers, educators must keep sessions short and focused, adapt to unexpected ward events, and utilize quiet moments between admissions for rapid teaching points. Flexibility and good time management ensure that education continues even in chaotic environments.
